Alex: Quick recap from this morning's multi-region failover dry run (us-west1 / us-east1 / eu-west1). Ran a mixed replay + synthetic spike to simulate region drain + client retries. Kernel selection was on auto, batching window=15ms, KV cache enabled. Observed ~1.8% SLO misses (p95/p99 inflation) during drain and fallback paths. Posting a few profiler snippets and notes below.

Priya: Nice. Can you paste the replay command + config you used?

Alex: Sure — replay harness + synthetic spike: 
```
./replay_harness --targets us-west1,us-east1,eu-west1 \
  --mode mixed_replay --replay-file ./captures/peak_weekday.json \
  --synthetic-rps 1200 --spike-duration 90s \
  --kernel-selection auto --batch-window-ms 15 --kv-cache on \
  --model-pin v1.3-quant8 --fallback-model v1.3-compat
```

Mateo: Was the model pinned on both primary and fallback? apples-to-apples baseline matters.

Alex: Yes — pinned to the exact checkpoints on all regions. Fallback model is functionally same weights but compiled w/o our fused attention kernels (that's the cheap fallback).

Jin: KV cache behavior during drain? warm vs cold state?

Alex: Good call — cache warmed before test, but we intentionally forced a region drain at t+60s which caused a bunch of requests to land in secondary region with a cold KV population. KV miss rate jumped from ~6% -> ~48% in the first 30s post-drain. That correlated with p99 token latency doubling on fallback path.

Sara: Can you paste the pctl numbers you observed? p50/p95/p99 for token latency and end-to-end?

Alex: snippet from console (percentiles in ms):
```
Region: us-west1 (primary) before drain: p50=18, p95=42, p99=76
Fallback region (cold kv) after drain: p50=34, p95=110, p99=260
Apples-to-apples baseline (no drain): p50=19, p95=45, p99=79
SLO target: p95 < 100ms, p99 < 200ms
SLO misses peaked at 1.8% overall, concentrated on fallback buckets
```

Priya: Oof p99 260 is rough. Do we know which ops/kernels dominated the extra time? profiler traces?

Alex: Yes — profiler shows a kernel selection fallback to generic matmul path for attention on the fallback compile. That single op added ~2.2ms per attention call which accumulates across long contexts. Also batching heuristics changed: smaller effective batch due to connection reshuffle during reroute -> batching efficiency dropped ~35%.

Jin: Can you share the flame sample? just the top 3 ops would help.

Alex: top ops (percent time):
```
1) attention_generic_matmul (fallback compile) ~34%
2) kv_cache_fetch (cold misses + network) ~22%
3) softmax_kernel (unfused) ~11%
```

Mateo: So two levers: (1) ensure fallback compiles include our fused attention kernels (or at least a closer performing kernel), (2) avoid cold KV on failover — maybe async KV prefetch on routing?

Sara: Also the batching behavior — when requests get re-routed we lose prefix affinity so continuous batching of similar seqlen drops. Could try batching window tweak or affinity-preserving routing.

Priya: Suggestion: rerun with kernel-selection=manual (force fused kernels on fallback) and batch-window-ms=8 to see low-latency tradeoff. Also run a cold-cache variant to measure worst-case.

Alex: Agreed. I'll queue two runs: (A) manual kernels + batch 8ms + warm KV, (B) auto kernels + batch 15ms + intentionally cold KV on secondary. We'll keep model pins identical.

infra-bot: Deploy note: replay job queued as job/8942 by Alex. ETA ~12m.

Jin: One more datapoint — router logs show ~12% of requests were re-routed to smaller instance types in eu-west1 during the spike because of capacity policy 'prefer_local_then_burst'. That increased RTT by ~45ms on average before server-side processing. Might be worth adjusting routing policy for critical SLOs.

Mateo: Can we do an apples-to-apples where we also equalize instance types (no cheap bursts) and equalize network RTT by adding artificial latency to local region to simulate inter-region? That isolates kernel+kv effects.

Alex: Good plan. Action items: 
- [ ] Run A: manual kernels + 8ms batch + warm KV (job/8942-A)
- [ ] Run B: auto kernels + 15ms batch + cold KV (job/8942-B)
- [ ] Run C: apples-to-apples equalized instances + artificial RTT to primary to isolate model/runtime effects
- [ ] Add short-term fix: add a small KV async-prefetch on routing code-path to populate prefix KV for likely reroutes

Sara: tagging @ops-team for routing policy tweak.

Priya: I'll collect the replay artifacts and diff the profiling traces — want to see op-level deltas. :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks team. Will post results in this thread and attach the run artifacts. :thinking:
